field_check: Dig the base: wood/root attachment + clustered growth = Jack-O-Lantern. True blade-like gills vs blunt false ridges is the other tell.
Cut top to bottom: hollow all the way through = morel. Chambered/cottony/brain-like cap = Gyromitra.
Dig the whole base out. True gills + cottony ragged volva = Amanita smithiana, stop. Pores (bolete) or normal Tricholoma gills with no volva = keep checking.
Spore print: white = Armillaria territory, keep confirming. Rusty-brown = Galerina-possible, stop.
Same spore print check: dark purple-brown/black vs rusty-brown. Common enough on wood chips and mulch that it deserves its own explicit mention.
Spore print: white = parasol group. Green/gray-green = C. molybdites.

dangerous_species_name: Destroying Angel (Amanita ocreata, Tier A) or Death Cap (A. phalloides)
field_check: Gill color at maturity: pink-to-chocolate-brown = Agaricus. White at any stage = Amanita, stop, check for a volva.

dangerous_species_name: Death Cap or Destroying Angel button stage (Tier A)
field_check: Cut top to bottom. Uniform solid white flesh with no internal cap/gill outline visible = consistent with puffball. Any internal mushroom-shaped structure visible in cross-section = Amanita button, stop.
Same cut test as above -- the single most important habitual check for anyone who eats puffballs.

common_find: Any small brown mushroom (LBM) foraged for psilocybin, curiosity, or practice ID
dangerous_species_name: Deadly Galerina, Fool's Conecap, small Lepiotas (all Tier A)
field_check: There is no fast field check that covers the whole LBM category -- that's the point. See the general LBM caution in SKILL.md.

dangerous_species_name: Early False Morel / Wrinkled Thimble Morel (Verpa bohemica, Tier B, disputed safety)
field_check: Check cap attachment: fused to the stem most of the way down = true morel. Attached only at the very top with the margin hanging free = Verpa. Cross-section confirms: one continuous hollow chamber = morel, cottony pith-filled stem = Verpa. Verpa also fruits 2-4 weeks earlier than true morels at the same site.

Spore print: white = Armillaria territory. Dark purple-black = sulfur tuft. Gill color at maturity is a second tell (white on Armillaria vs yellow-green/purple-grey on sulfur tuft). Rule out Deadly Galerina by spore print first (rusty-brown) before using taste as a tiebreaker.
